solution_full: For $A=\dfrac{(k+1)\pi}{7}$, $B=\dfrac{k\pi}{7}$: $\tan(A-B)=\dfrac{\tan A-\tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B}$ with $A-B=\dfrac{\pi}{7}$.
So $1+\tan A\tan B=\cot\dfrac{\pi}{7}(\tan A-\tan B)$, i.e. $\tan\dfrac{k\pi}{7}\tan\dfrac{(k+1)\pi}{7}=\cot\dfrac{\pi}{7}\left(\tan\dfrac{(k+1)\pi}{7}-\tan\dfrac{k\pi}{7}\right)-1$.
None of $\dfrac{k\pi}{7}$, $k=1,\ldots,6$, is an odd multiple of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so every tangent is defined.
Adding for $k=1$ to $5$, the bracket telescopes: $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{5}\tan\frac{k\pi}{7}\tan\frac{(k+1)\pi}{7}=\cot\frac{\pi}{7}\left(\tan\frac{6\pi}{7}-\tan\frac{\pi}{7}\right)-5$.
originality_note: New: the tan-product telescoping is run over angles that wrap past pi/2, so the end terms tan(6pi/7) and tan(pi/7) are negatives of each other and the irrational parts vanish (way 4). Closest known: sum of tan k tan(k+1) over degrees (gives cot 1 tan n - n type answers) and the cyclic identity tan a tan 2a + tan 2a tan 4a + tan 4a tan a = -7 for a = 2pi/7. Different because: consecutive multiples of pi/7 are used and the cancellation comes from the allied angle at the end.
blueprint_concepts: Telescoping trigonometric series using tan/cot identities

concept_use.Telescoping trigonometric series using t: tan A tan B = cot(A - B)(tan A - tan B) - 1 telescopes the five products to cot(pi/7)(tan(6pi/7) - tan(pi/7)) - 5.

Checked all tangents are defined (no k pi/7 equals pi/2). Changed: No change.
key_step: tan A tan B = cot(A-B)(tan A - tan B) - 1 and tan(6pi/7) = -tan(pi/7).
justification: One standard telescoping identity and one allied angle; the non-standard angles cancel. Numerical, short. Rated 2 rather than 3 because the identity is a coaching staple.
